title: Changing mop heads and pads, and treating heel marks
audience: Cleaners who change wet and dust mop heads and microfiber pads during floor work, and who deal with marks on hard floors.
learningOutcomes: Remove a dirty bucket mop head and fit a clean one, using the clamp type on the handle.
Remove a microfiber pad from a flat mop holder and attach a clean one without contamination.
Choose a method for heel marks that does not scratch the floor, and test it before full use.

instruction.heading: Why heads and pads are changed, not just rinsed
instruction.body: A mop head that is full of soil or has dried with residue will put that soil back onto the floor during the next room. Changing it between rooms, or when it is visibly soiled, keeps the clean floor clean. The change must be done in a way that does not contaminate the clean head or the handle. Gloves are required for every change, because the head is in direct contact with the soil and the cleaner's hands.

instruction.heading: Bucket mop heads: the clamp types
instruction.body: Bucket mop heads are held on the handle by one of several clamp types. Some use a jaw collar that tightens around the head. Others use a spring-loaded bar that is pressed against the handle, a wing-nut bracket, or a locking wheel that holds a plastic bar against the head. Before changing a head, identify the clamp type. Loosen the clamp, slide the soiled head off, and bag it for laundering. Seat the new head where the clamp grips it and tighten until it is held firm. Give the head a tug to check it does not slip.

instruction.heading: Flat mop pads: the hook-and-loop attachment
instruction.body: Flat mop pads attach to the holder with a hook-and-loop backing. To take off a soiled pad, pin the pad down with one foot and steady the holder with the other, then lift the holder so the backing lets go. Once it has come loose, turn the holder a quarter turn and use its tip to lift the pad clear, then bag it. To fit a fresh pad, lay it flat and press the holder squarely onto it so the hook surface grips. Check that the pad is square before use.

instruction.heading: Dealing with heel marks
instruction.body: Heel marks are black scuffs left by shoes on vinyl and similar floors. They are usually lifted with a gentle method first, and the mop head should be the first tool used. Clip a white, non-abrasive pad onto the head to lift scuffs during the wet pass. As an alternative, work a soft pad over the scuffs before the wet pass begins. Test any method in a small area first, and check that it does not dull or mark the floor. Do not use a harsh scouring pad on a floor that has a sealed finish, because it can remove the finish. If the marks do not lift, report the floor to the supervisor.

procedure: Put on gloves before touching any head or pad.
Identify the mop head clamp type, or the flat pad fastening, before you start.
For a bucket head, loosen the clamp, take off the soiled head, and bag it.
Fit the clean head, tighten the clamp, and tug the head to check it is secure.
For a flat pad, peel the dirty pad from the holder, lift it by the holder, and bag it.
Press a clean pad onto the holder, centring it so the hook-and-loop grips fully.
For scuffs, test a gentle pad in a small area first, then use it before the wet pass.
Store the dirty heads and pads for laundering and clean the holders before reuse.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner is asked to lift black heel scuffs from a vinyl corridor. The cleaner fits a coarse scouring pad to the mop head and scrubs hard.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the risk, and what should the cleaner do instead?
workedExamples.reasoning: A coarse scouring pad can dull or scratch the floor and remove its finish, which is harder to repair than the heel marks. Test a white non-abrasive pad in a small area first. If it does not lift the marks, report the floor to the supervisor instead of trying a stronger abrasive.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner pulls a flat pad off the holder by hand and presses a new one on while still wearing the same gloves that handled the floor.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should have been done differently?
workedExamples.reasoning: Change gloves or wear a fresh pair before handling a clean pad, and bag the dirty pad rather than dropping it on the floor. Handling the clean pad with contaminated gloves transfers soil to it.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves, changed or refreshed before handling clean heads and pads.
Spare bucket mop heads with clamps, and microfiber flat pads.
Laundry bags for dirty heads and pads.
White non-abrasive scrub pad for heel marks.
Bucket and wringer, or charging bucket, for loading clean pads.

commonErrors.error: Reusing a dirty head or pad on the next room because it still looks clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Change heads and pads between rooms and when they are visibly soiled.

commonErrors.error: Using a scouring pad on heel marks without testing.
commonErrors.prevention: Test a gentle method in a small area first, and report marks that do not lift.

commonErrors.error: Putting a clean pad on the holder without centring it, so it slides and gaps.
commonErrors.prevention: Centre the holder on the pad and press all round, checking the grip before use.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Wear gloves for every head or pad change, because soil on the head can reach your skin.
Check the clamp and the holder before use. A loose head can fly off during mopping and cause a slip or a strain.

qualityStandard: Each mop head or pad is clean before it contacts the floor.
The clamp or hook-and-loop attachment holds the head or pad firmly with no slip.
Heel marks are removed without scratches or dull patches on the floor.
Dirty heads and pads are bagged for laundering and not left on the floor.
documentationEvidence: Record of the number of heads and pads changed, where the site tracks laundry.
Note of any floor where heel marks did not lift, for supervisor review.
summary: Change heads and pads between rooms and when they are soiled.
Identify the clamp type or hook-and-loop fitting before you start.
Start heel-mark treatment with a gentle non-abrasive method and test it first.
Keep dirty heads and pads bagged, and wear clean gloves for the clean fit.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the first step before changing a bucket mop head?
options: Soak the head in the charging bucket for an hour
Identify the clamp type on the handle and release it
Cut the head off the handle with scissors today

knowledgeChecks.question: How should heel marks be treated on a vinyl corridor floor?
options: Scrub hard with a coarse scouring pad across the whole corridor
Apply strong solvent to the marks and leave it overnight
Test a gentle non-abrasive method in a small area, then treat the marks

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should dirty mop heads and pads be placed in a bag rather than on the floor?
options: So that soil from them does not spread to clean surfaces or to the clean heads
Because bags are needed for the pads to dry faster and the bags keep the floor clear
Because mop heads must be stored on the floor to dry out faster
